items.summary: The only way to avoid Google's requirement is to pull your apps from Europe and the UK.

New Play Store requirements force app developers to publish their addresses online

The only way to avoid Google's requirement is to pull your apps from Europe and the UK.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 6:00 AM ET

•

•

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google is reportedly facing privacy concerns over a requirement for app developers to disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses.

• The requirement applies to all app developers, including solo creators, who offer their apps in Europe and the UK.

• The company won’t allow developers to use a PO box, leading at least one creator to say they might rent a separate office.

Google and partners started rolling out developer verification for Android apps earlier this year, along with a more convoluted sideloading process on devices. These new measures will launch globally in January, but another Google requirement is under scrutiny due to privacy issues.

The Elec reports that Google is facing privacy concerns over a recent requirement that app developers (including solo creators) publicly disclose their phone numbers and physical addresses on Google Play. This move, which kicks in from March 2027, is meant to help Google and developers comply with European regulatory requirements. However, the outlet adds that developer addresses and phone numbers will be shown worldwide.

Readers' poll

Do you think app developers should publicly list their address on Google Play?

13 votes

“I don’t need a separate office to develop and operate games, but I’m considering renting one to protect my personal information,” an independent developer was quoted as saying by The Elec. “Disclosing developers’ home addresses amounts to an invasion of privacy.”

A step too far for individual developers?

These requirements are related to Google’s trade status declaration process. The company explained in a support page last month that “all active developer accounts” distributing apps in Europe or the UK need to declare whether they are a trader or non-trader by February 1, 2027. Google notes that developers should declare themselves as traders if they have ad-supported apps, paid apps, or apps with in-app purchases. Those who declare themselves as traders will have their address and phone number publicly displayed. However, the search giant clarifies that developers who don’t offer their apps in Europe or the UK can declare themselves a non-trader, presumably avoiding the public address and phone number requirement.

Google also explicitly notes in its support page that phone numbers and addresses of personal developer accounts will be publicly shown:

If you use a personal developer account, you must provide a contact phone number to be displayed on Google Play. Be aware that your address will also be publicly displayed.

An Australian developer used Google’s support forum to complain about these disclosure requirements:

I’m a solo developer in Australia with a personal account and one small app (a single paying subscriber). To comply with the trader declaration, I’d have to publish my home address and phone number to users worldwide from March 2027. Support confirmed PO Boxes aren’t accepted, since the address must match my verified residential address.
The law behind this (EU DSA / UK DMCCA) only requires disclosure to EEA and UK consumers, yet Google is choosing to display these details globally. My only privacy-safe option is to withdraw my app from 31 countries and declare as a non-trader.

“Publishing a home address is a real safety risk for solo developers, especially those working from home,” the Australian developer added. “I’d love to stay available in the EU and UK, but not at the cost of my personal safety.”

Developers have also taken to Reddit to criticize the publication of addresses, with one user claiming that Google was “backing developers into a corner.” Another user warned that bad actors could scrape Google Play to get every developer’s address and phone number.

In any event, we’ve asked Google for comment regarding this matter and whether it’ll allow PO boxes in response to privacy concerns. We’ll update the article as soon as the company gets back to us. I can certainly understand displaying a phone number as an alternative to email support, but forcing individual developers to publicly share their physical address seems like a step too far.

items.title: Here are the best T-Mobile T-Mix perks to choose (and what to avoid)
items.summary: Not every T-Mix perk is worth it, but there are a few that stand above the rest.
items.body:

Mobile

Here are the best T-Mobile T-Mix perks to choose (and what to avoid)

Not every T-Mix perk is worth it, but there are a few that stand above the rest.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 5:00 AM ET

•

•

T-Mobile

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

The new T-Mix plans are here, though we’ve already concluded that for most users there are probably better options out there. For those who aren’t aware, the new T-Mix plans drop extras like free T-Satellite access, streaming services, or even special free phone deals. Instead, each plan gives you a certain amount of points that you can use in combination to pick streaming services, phone offers, and more.

If you absolutely have your heart set on a T-Mix plan, you’ll at least want to make the best of the perks available. Let’s jump in and look at the best perks available, as well as ones you might want to avoid.

What are the best perks available on T-Mix?

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

One of the most important things to know is that not all T-Mobile T-Mix perks are of equal value. Some perks cost multiple “pick” points, and even within similar categories, the actual retail value can vary wildly. From a purely cost-value perspective, the three best perks are Apple TV ($14.99/month), Hulu with Ads ($12.49/month), and SiriusXM All Access ($11.99/month). Just keep in mind that Apple TV’s one-pick price is a limited-time deal: it costs one pick through June 2027, then jumps to two picks.

Of course, what apps and services you use comes down to personal preferences. While the three above are a good deal because they only cost one pick each and have values above $10, here are some of the other solid options for 1-pick perks:

• Paramount Plus Essential – $8.99

• Netflix Standard with Ads – $8.99

• YouTube Premium Lite – $8.99

• DashPass by DoorDash – $9.99

• Google AI Plus 2TB – $9.99

• T-Sat – $10

Beyond the 1-pick offers, the value gets a little less impressive if I’m honest. Most 2-pick offers range in value from $11.99 to $19.99, with only a few like Google AI Pro ($19.99 monthly value) really worth it. The same applies to the few 3- and 4-pick perks, which range from $19.99 to $31.99 in monthly value.

Generally speaking, the best deals are for movie and TV streaming. Music streaming perks tend to cost a lot more points, though SiriusXM is a rare exception. It’s also worth noting this only gives you app access, so there’s no built-in car sat radio support with this plan.

In addition to streaming perks and other subscription services, you can also use your picks to activate phone deals. The actual value of these options ranges dramatically and can take anywhere from one to four pick points. Don’t assume all low-point offers are low value, either. For example, both the Moto G (2026) and Moto Razr cost a single pick point, despite the latter being a much more expensive device.

Which perks are best avoided?

Taylor Kerns / Android Authority

Above, we talked about some of the perks that we feel are worth it, but are there any that are worth avoiding? For my vote, I’d say Delta Air Lines points and Pandora Plus are at the top of the list. Both use one pick each and have values right around $5-6, which means you’re better saying your perk points for something else.

Honestly, the same goes for Apple Music Individual ($11.99 monthly value) and Pandora Premium ($11.99 monthly value). These both use two pick points each and yet have values similar to many of the better one-pick choices like Apple TV.

Are these T-Mix plans even worth it for the Picks/Perks?

T-Mobile

Keep in mind this is far from a comprehensive look at every perk, and there could certainly be a few others worth looking at.

Maybe you aren’t into movies and TV and prefer to use up three points on Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($22.99) or use four picks on ESPN Unlimited ($31.99). These might not be great in the cost-to-value department on paper, but if you aren’t going to use the others and have points left to spend? Why not.

The biggest thing to remember is that in nearly every case the combined value of plan features and perks will still be more expensive than if you went with a prepaid plan or stuck with a better legacy postpaid plan. For those who aren’t already on a legacy plan and are unwilling to give prepaid a try, it could still be worth it; just don’t go in expecting to get a great value here.

items.summary: Three wake words, one surprisingly close reader poll.
items.body:

Smart homeVirtual assistants

Hey Google remains readers’ favorite wake word, but a new option is catching up fast

Three wake words, one surprisingly close reader poll.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 4:28 AM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

For what feels like decades, “OK Google” activated the company’s various smart home, voice assistant, and audio-triggered features. Then came “Hey Google,” and the two lived in harmony for several years. However, there’s a new wake word that Google wants to sear into your memory. Starting with Intelligent Eyewear, “Hey Gemini” will be the preferred trigger word for Android XR. While the old phrase will still work, Google is actively guiding users to involve its newer voice assistant when summoning your digital pal.

Naturally, adapting what has now become muscle memory will be difficult for many, many users — me included. We asked readers what their preferred Google wake word is in a recent survey, and here are the results:

Poll results

What's your Google wake word of choice?

41.1%Hey Google

1. Hey Google880 votes41.1%

2. Hey Gemini644 votes30.0%

3. OK Google620 votes28.9%

2,144 votes · androidauthority.com · results as of November 26, 2026

With 41.1% of the vote, “Hey Google” is our readers’ preferred way to trigger Google’s audio assistant and features. Surprisingly, 30% of readers side with “Hey Gemini,” while 28.9% use the older “OK Google” hotword.

That’s a surprisingly even spread across the three options available and suggests that users prefer having a choice rather than being prescribed a way to use their devices.

For some, “Hey Google” just rolls off the tongue. Memory certainly plays a role for users who prefer this option, too.

Gemini doesn't roll off the tongue as smooth as Google.

Hey Google, has been stamped into my everyday life, for years. Change is never easy but, I think Hey Gemini, will come out on top. Though, I'd rather be able to customize my "wake" word. As I'm able to do with Bixby. "Yo Homie," wakes my Tab S9+.

Others believe “Hey Gemini” is a better fit to summon the actual assistant rather than the company behind it.

Saying "Hey Gemini" is much more relaxed, personal and down to earth, than saying the very commercial and very artificial "Hey Google". I don't want to talk to a company name - I wanna talk to gentle and friendly assistant. It makes it much more human and natural.

Hey Google sounds like to the browser. When talking to Gemini I would like to call it by name

Some argue that only one word should wake Gemini: Gemini.

Keith · Nov 25, 2026

Why not just "Gemini"?
I thought the old rule used to be 3 syllables, 2 words or 1.
I don't think Gemini is a word too many people say very often which would unintentionally wake it up and if they do just don't use that
And btw why is this site so riddled with pop-up ads on the chrome browser?

On Google is officially entering its 'Hey Gemini' era

View in conversation →

Meanwhile, “Hey Gemini” is far less likely to accidentally trigger activations, according to others.

Editor's pick

phil.ferrar · Nov 15, 2026

Easy to remember and unlikely to be triggered by mistake (by other audio devices) as often as the earlier two were.

Who knew picking an assistant wake word was such a personal choice?

The Blurams F20C solar camera sees what my video doorbell misses

This outdoor security camera was able to solve my problem.

Brought to you by Blurams

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 4:22 AM ET

•

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

My doorbell camera works great at showing who’s at my front door. However, it leaves me with a couple of blind spots. First, it doesn’t show my package at the bottom of the door when it’s delivered. If I’m not home, that package might sit there for hours, making it vulnerable to theft by a porch pirate. My low-tech solution was to put a sign under the door asking the driver to place the package into a box next to my door. However, this creates a second blind spot because my doorbell camera doesn’t show packages going into the box.

With the Blurams F20C 4K Solar Outdoor Security Camera, my goal was to eliminate these two blind spots. I mounted it to a tree that faces my front door so I can see if the driver leaves the package at the front door or if they put it into the delivery box. So, is a solar-powered camera with no wires reliable enough to keep watch over my deliveries all day?

Why a doorbell camera isn’t the best solution to track package deliveries

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

A lot of people buy a doorbell camera to track their online deliveries. In my experience, they leave out a lot. Not only do they have a fixed angle that’s usually pointed at face height, but they also tend to record short clips only after motion triggers them. This problem arises because traditional motion-triggered cameras use a PIR sensor. This means that they wake up when movement is detected. In theory, this sounds smart, but in reality, I noticed that most clips start late and end early, leaving homeowners like me both frustrated and anxious.

The F20C takes a different approach, which I’ll explain later in more detail. Let’s start with the basics first.

What’s in the box

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

Inside the box, you’ll find the 4K Ultra HD camera, a solar panel, mounting hardware, and screw packs.

The F20C has a 5W solar panel, a large 12,000mAh battery, and it supports local storage on a microSD card up to 512GB. That means you’re not forced into a monthly cloud plan to store and watch your footage, like with some of its competitors. Extended cloud storage is optional, with free single-day cloud storage also available. It has an IP66 waterproof rating, making it rain, snow, and dust resistant, so you can leave it out without a problem. It supports both 2.4GHz and 5GHz WiFi 6 connections for outdoor monitoring.

Setup is very DIY friendly

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

After downloading the Blurams app, setup took only about 5 minutes. You simply pick the F20C from the selection of Blurams cameras and follow the app instructions to connect it to the app.

The physical install is where things got interesting. At first, I installed it on a wooden post facing my front door. I installed the mounting bracket with two screws and slid the camera into the slot. Later, I decided to mount it on a tree closer to my front door instead. This gave me a much better viewing angle of my front gate, the walkway, and front door with the 360° Pan and 90° tilt feature.

The F20C supports two solar setups. The panel can attach directly to the camera to make it a single unit. Alternatively, if there is a better area that gets more sunlight, the solar panel can be detached and mounted in a separate location. The panel has a long 3-meter USB-C cable to enable this. For aesthetic reasons, I mounted it as a single unit, but if I were running out of power, I was prepared to move the solar panel to the other side of the tree. So far, it’s worked perfectly as a single unit, but things may change as we get into the shorter days of winter.

It comes with a free trial for cloud storage

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The F20C comes with a free one-month trial of Blurams’ Basic cloud plan for one camera. It stores either seven days of 24/7 continuous recording or 15 days of motion-triggered clips. The plan also includes Smart Detection, which can tell the difference between people, vehicles, and packages, so you get fewer false alarms. While package detection is part of the paid cloud service, a free on-device package detection will be introduced in a future update. This will filter package-related events without requiring a subscription. You also get rich notifications, which show a snapshot right on your lock screen.

Once the trial ends, you still get some free cloud features. This includes motion and sound alerts, event snapshots, and 12-second event recordings that are stored for one day. That’s not much, so I installed a microSD card to record footage locally. If you don’t want to pay for a monthly cloud plan, I recommend doing the same.

AOV vs PIR: No missing moments

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

AOV stands for Always-on Video, and it’s Blurams’ low-power continuous recording approach. Instead of sleeping until the motion sensor wakes it, the camera stays in a low-power state and records the entire time. PIR (passive infrared) cameras only wake up when they detect a change in infrared heat, which is why their clips often miss the start. With AOV, there’s no gap at the beginning of a clip, and nothing cut off at the end. Having now tried both types of cameras, I definitely prefer AOV cameras because they provide a full video timeline.

What it caught at my front door

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

This is the part I cared about most. Before the F20C, I already knew packages were arriving because of the alerts my doorbell camera provided. But the doorbell clips were never perfect. They either started too late, after the driver had already reached the door, or cut out too early.

Now, I can see the whole sequence. With the Smart AI detection, Always-on Video (AOV), and pan/tilt/zoom (PTZ), I saw the delivery driver open the front gate, walk to the door, read the sign on the bottom, and place the package into the box. This is the peace of mind I was hoping to get from my video doorbell. With the F20C, all the blind spots were eliminated.

To date, I haven’t had a single package stolen. But the F20C did capture something I wasn’t expecting. One evening, while I was working in my home office, I got a notification from both my video doorbell camera and the Blurams F20C. I looked at the footage on my doorbell camera and saw someone walk up to my door. Unfortunately, the doorbell camera stopped recording once they got to the door. I immediately opened the Blurams app and watched that footage. This person was walking down the sidewalk, saw the sign under the door, and mistook it for a package. As soon as he got to the door, he realized it was just a sign. He turned around and left empty-handed.

To reiterate, my doorbell camera only saw him arrive. The F20C saw what he was looking at, and showed him walking away afterwards. I saw the entire sequence in a single video clip. That’s the kind of context a single doorbell camera angle can’t give you. Right then and there, it convinced me that a backup camera on the front door was a great idea.

Video quality, day and night

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The F20C records up to 4K Ultra HD at 2160p resolution, but users can adjust it to Full High Definition (FHD) at 1296p, or High Definition (HD) at 720p. Higher video quality requires more internet bandwidth, so I keep it at FHD to be safe.

Users have several options for night vision to choose from. This is something I haven’t seen in other security cameras. IR Night Vision provides night vision mode in black and white. This is the ideal setting for viewing longer distances. Intelligent Night Vision provides a black and white image when no motion is detected. However, when motion is detected, the video automatically shifts into full color mode. Another option is Color Night Vision, which turns on the white light when the F20C enters night vision mode. Finally, Forced Night Vision enables black and white night vision mode without being affected by the light environment.

I set the F20C to Intelligent Night Vision, which I feel is the best all-around setting for most users. In this setting, the white light will turn off with a delay after the motion stops.

Smart alerts to prevent notification overload

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The last thing anyone wants from an outdoor security camera is unnecessary notifications. The F20C uses on-device AI to recognize humans, pets, vehicles, and packages through a paid cloud service plan. A future update will soon provide on-device AI package detection for free. This provides context to any notification alerts. Users can also set a schedule for receiving notifications. Since I’m using this to track package deliveries, I’m keeping the F20C armed with Human Detection enabled so it only starts recording when a human event is detected. If my neighbor’s cat comes into frame, I will not receive a notification.

There’s also a dedicated Package Detection alert notification that will soon be free after a future update. With a paid cloud subscription, users can also enable rich notification alerts for packages. I’m considering a paid cloud subscription for rich notifications since tracking packages is the primary reason I’ve installed the F20C.

Users can also enable a Perimeter Alarm and specify the alert period. I set the alarm to turn on between 10pm and 4am for any Human detection during the night. If someone comes into my front yard during the night, a sound alert will go on 5 times along with a flashing light alert for 10 seconds. This acts as a deterrent for any thief trying to break into my house.

Should you buy the Blurams F20C?

Andy Baryer / Android Authority

The whole point of reviewing this camera was to see if it can solve a specific problem I have with package deliveries. Did the delivery driver place it on the ground, or follow my instructions to place it in the box beside my door? The F20C solved it. To my surprise, it also caught someone looking for a package that wasn’t there.

The Blurams F20C is a good fit for homeowners who want to store and review footage without paying a subscription plan. You get a lot of peace of mind with this product. It’s DIY friendly because you don’t have to fiddle around with wires or connect it to a power source. With solar charging, it can be placed virtually anywhere without worrying about charging it again. What impressed me the most is how it records the whole event instead of fragmented clips that start too late or end too early. That alone makes this camera easy to recommend.

My advice is to take advantage of the Black Friday deals. The F20C is currently available for $65.99, down from $149.99. You can also get two of them for $121.99. The company also has deals available on its cloud storage plans, if you’re interested in them. The promotion period runs from November 19 to November 30th.

After Black Friday and Cyber Monday, Android Authority readers can still get these exclusive savings on Amazon from November 19 to December 31. Use Discount Code: AAUSFC1P for the 1-Pack and AAUSFC2P for the 2-Pack.

If you’ve been thinking about getting a home security camera, take advantage of these Black Friday deals for the F20C and the cloud storage. There’s peace of mind knowing you’ll have footage of any event that matters to you.

items.summary: You don't need to upgrade your phone to get the latest Samsung security feature.
items.body:

MobileAndroid apps

Here’s how to get app lock on your Android phone right now

You don't need to upgrade your phone to get the latest Samsung security feature.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 4:00 AM ET

•

•

Andy Walker / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

Samsung’s One UI 9.5 update brought some exciting feature additions to supported Galaxy smartphones, but perhaps the most exciting for me is the ability to lock apps behind a password or biometric data, keeping information away from prying eyes.

While those running the latest Android 17 QPR3 beta build also have access to app lock smarts, most Android users have no access to it, and likely never will unless they upgrade. But, thankfully, there’s a free, open-source solution to this problem. It’s simply called AppLock Revived, and it’s the easiest way to bring Samsung’s latest security feature to your Android phone.

What is AppLock Revived, and how do you install it?

Andy Walker / Android Authority

AppLock Revived is a fork of the legacy AppLock project on GitHub, which was my personal app-locking solution for several months. However, since it’s no longer regularly maintained, I turned to one of its starred forks. Revived continues App Lock’s core functionality, but adds more polish, a Material 3 Expressive coat, and several additional features that further enhance the experience.

Readers' poll

Which apps do you feel need a secondary lock the most?

0 votes

Let’s start right at the top. Setting up AppLock Revived might seem a little daunting, but the app handholds users through the entire process. Since it’s not listed on the Google Play Store, you’ll need to grab it directly from GitHub.

In short, you have two options to accomplish this. The first is downloading its APK directly from its GitHub repository. The second is using an app updater like Obtainium. The latter is my preferred method since it also ensures that this security-critical app remains updated.

How to install AppLock Revived through Obtainium:

1. Visit the official Obtainium website and tap the Download Universal APK button to download its latest version.

2. Once downloaded, install Obtainium. You may need to enable Install unknown apps.

3. Next, open Obtainium, tap + Add, and paste AppLock Revived’s GitHub address (https://github.com/riyadmondol2006/AppLock-Revived) in the App source URL field. Tap the + button.

4. Tap Install.

Once installed, you’ll be asked to enable various settings and verify some required permissions, including the option to Display over other apps and skirt battery optimization.

AppLock Revived features and functionality

Andy Walker / Android Authority

AppLock Revived, like the app it’s based on, offers users three distinct implementations: using Android’s Accessibility service, using Android’s usage statistics, or using Shizuku. The latter requires its own installation method, so if you’re just giving AppLock Revived a try, pick the first option.

Users can add as many apps to the lock list as desired, and AppLock Revived makes this process as simple as flicking a toggle. There are also distinct per-app settings, too, allowing more control over which unlock level is required. I particularly like the Two-step option, which uses both biometrics and PIN to unlock the app. Users can also lump apps into profiles — Home, Work, Guest, or user-created profiles — and set default unlock durations and options within these baskets.

Digging a little deeper into available settings, AppLock Revived also includes Trigger exclusions, which stops apps from relocking if jumping from one locked app to another, and uninstallation protection, which stops selected apps from being uninstalled without verification. Users can also set specific unlock time durations, failed attempt lockouts, enable a Scramble PIN keypad option to prevent spying, lock newly installed apps, lock away the photo and file picker on Android, and Close locked apps when the screen turns off.

I also appreciate the Intruder selfie feature. AppLock Revived will take a selfie shot if incorrect unlock credentials are entered. It’s triggered by a predetermined number of failed attempts, and users can view those selfies in the app, too. All of these little additions go beyond the original App Lock app and, in some cases, beyond Samsung’s solution.

Should you install AppLock Revived on your phone?

Andy Walker / Android Authority

Unfortunately, if you were hoping for complete feature parity with One UI 9.5, you’ll be left feeling shortchanged. Since AppLock Revived is a third-party Android app and not a native Samsung or Android feature, it does miss out on a few features.

For one, it doesn’t remove locked apps or their widgets from your home screen. Since I use a third-party launcher, this isn’t much of an issue for me. Notifications also persist, and there’s seemingly no option in AppLock Revived to suppress them. Again, it’s not a game-breaker, but it does highlight that the native app lock might have the edge for some users.

Either way, AppLock Revived is an open-source app that brings a cutting-edge Android feature to older devices for free. Given that Google has confirmed native app lock won’t come to older Android versions, this is the easiest way to get a similar feature on your device right now.

Digging a little deeper into available settings, AppLock Revived also includes Trigger exclusions, which stops apps from relocking if jumping from one locked app to another, and uninstallation protection, which stops selected apps from being uninstalled without verification. Users can also set specific unlock time durations, failed attempt lockouts, enable a Scramble PIN keypad option to prevent spying, lock newly installed apps, lock away the photo and file picker on Android, and Close locked apps when the screen turns off.

I also appreciate the Intruder selfie feature. AppLock Revived will take a selfie shot if incorrect unlock credentials are entered. It’s triggered by a predetermined number of failed attempts, and users can view those selfies in the app, too. All of these little additions go beyond the original App Lock app and, in some cases, beyond Samsung’s solution.

Unfortunately, if you were hoping for complete feature parity with One UI 9.5, you’ll be left feeling shortchanged. Since AppLock Revived is a third-party Android app and not a native Samsung or Android feature, it does miss out on a few features.

For one, it doesn’t remove locked apps or their widgets from your home screen. Since I use a third-party launcher, this isn’t much of an issue for me. Again, it’s not a game-breaker, but it does highlight that the native app lock might have the edge for some users.

Either way, AppLock Revived is an open-source app that brings a cutting-edge Android feature to older devices for free. Given that Google has confirmed native app lock won’t come to older Android versions, this is the easiest way to get a similar feature on your device right now.

Samsung is killing Quick Share’s Private sharing, and it’s already gone in One UI 9.5 beta

A Galaxy Store update warns of the upcoming shutdown, while One UI 9.5 Beta 1 removes the toggle and code entirely.

TL;DR

• Samsung has added an advance notice to the Galaxy Store changelog for Quick Share version 13.9.10.5 warning that it plans to discontinue the Private sharing feature.

• Once the shutdown takes effect, users will not be able to send or receive files through Private sharing, and recipients will lose access to previously shared files.

• Samsung has not announced a specific cutoff date, though the toggle and code are already removed in Quick Share v13.9.50.30 on One UI 9.5 Beta 1 on the Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Samsung’s Quick Share has evolved rapidly this year, gaining features like AirDrop compatibility on the Galaxy S26 series and preparing for Tap to Share in One UI 9.5. However, not every tool is making the cut. Samsung is now officially warning users that it plans to discontinue Quick Share’s Private sharing feature.

The warning appears in the Galaxy Store changelog for Quick Share version 13.9.10.5, which lists an “Advance notice of the upcoming discontinuation of the ‘Private sharing’ feature”.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

This follows an earlier discovery by SammyGuru, which spotted an in-app string reading, “Private sharing will end on %s,” while Reddit users have also begun flagging the Galaxy Store update notice.

On our Galaxy S26 Ultra running One UI 9.5 Beta 1, the feature is already gone. There’s no Private sharing toggle in Quick Share, and the strings and code behind the feature have been removed from the app, which jumped to 13.9.50.30 in the beta. Samsung’s One UI 9.5 beta changelog doesn’t mention the removal.

Private sharing within Quick Share was designed to give Galaxy owners tighter control over sensitive files sent to other Galaxy devices. Instead of relying on standard local transfers, the feature encrypted files through blockchain technology and let senders set expiration dates, revoke access remotely, and block recipients from saving, forwarding, or taking screenshots of the shared content.

According to the in-app strings, shutting down the feature means users will no longer be able to send or receive files through Private sharing once the cutoff arrives. More importantly, recipients will also lose access to any files previously shared with them through the mode. Standard Quick Share transfers between Android, Windows, and supported iOS devices should remain unaffected.

Samsung has not yet announced an exact shutdown date: the code currently uses a placeholder, and Quick Share also displays no notice yet. However, publishing an advance notice directly in the public Galaxy Store changelog signals that the end is approaching soon.

If you rely on Private sharing to access sensitive documents or media sent by others, you should make alternative arrangements before Samsung flips the switch.

• The feature, called Keep audio in headphones, should appear in Connection preferences once it goes live.

Google could soon make one small but useful change to how Android handles Bluetooth audio. We’ve spotted a new feature in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 that could let users keep audio playing through their headphones even when another audio device, such as a car stereo or Bluetooth speaker, connects to their phone.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We spotted the feature, called “Keep audio in headphones,” in the latest Android 17 QPR3 Beta 4 build. The setting comes with a straightforward description: “Always play audio in your headphones when other audio devices like speakers and cars connect to this device.”

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

We found and enabled the toggle under Settings > Connected devices > Connection preferences. We’ve enabled it manually in the beta, so it’s worth noting that the feature isn’t necessarily available to everyone running the current build just yet.

The feature should be particularly handy for anyone who regularly uses wireless headphones alongside other Bluetooth audio devices. For instance, imagine listening to music through your earbuds when you get into your car. Your phone might normally switch audio output to the car’s infotainment system once it connects. With this setting enabled, Android should keep playback routed through your headphones instead.

It’s a small improvement, but one that could save users from having to manually switch audio outputs every time another Bluetooth device connects.

items.summary: Making a call without unfolding your Razr just got harder.
items.body:

Mobile

Motorola's Android 17 update breaks cover screen calling features for some Razr users

Making a call without unfolding your Razr just got harder.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 3:07 AM ET

•

•

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Some Motorola Razr users report losing access to the dial pad and contacts on the cover screen after updating to Android 17.

• The issue appears to stem from Motorola replacing its native Phone app with Google’s, with no easy way to switch back.

• Rotating the phone or reducing the display and font sizes has helped some affected users restore the missing functionality.

One of the biggest selling points of Motorola’s Razr phones is how much you can do without ever unfolding them. We’ve previously put this versatility to the test, but something as basic as making a phone call from the cover screen is now proving difficult for some Razr owners following the Android 17 update.

Affected users say the update replaced Motorola’s native Phone app with Google’s alternative. While the new app works as expected on the main display, the cover screen experience is different. Users report that they can still access recent calls but can no longer open the dial pad or access contacts without opening the phone.

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Razr owners in a Reddit discussion say the switch to Google’s Phone app brought the welcome addition of visual voicemail, but at the expense of the cover screen dialer and full-screen calling interface. As a result, they now have to unlock their phone just to see who’s calling, instead of having the caller ID appear across the cover screen as before.

A Razr 50 Ultra (Razr Ultra 2024) owner on Motorola’s community forum describes a similar experience, saying Google’s app doesn’t scale properly on the cover screen, making it difficult to dial numbers. The user also says there’s no option to switch back to Motorola’s app through the phone’s default app settings.

Similar complaints have surfaced on the Google Play Store, where Razr owners have reported degraded functionality and poor scaling on the external display as recently as November 25. In response to one complaint, Google suggested the problem was device-specific and advised the affected user to contact Motorola.

Google Play Store

This isn’t the first time Razr owners have experienced compatibility issues with Google’s Phone app. Similar complaints date back to Android 16, but the apparent inability to switch back to Motorola’s own app following the Android 17 update leaves affected users with fewer options.

There is some good news, though. One affected owner discovered that rotating the cover screen brings back the missing Home and Dial buttons. Another recently reported success by reducing the font and display sizes under Settings > Display size & text. This suggests that at least some of the missing functionality could be down to how the app scales on the smaller display.

With Motorola’s Android 17 rollout reaching more Razr models, hopefully, Motorola and Google can iron out these compatibility issues before more owners find themselves unfolding their phones just to dial a number.

Poll: Is text selection still too finicky on Android phones?

Selecting text on Android always feels more miss than hit.

This week, I encountered a Reddit post that made me feel seen. I genuinely thought I was one of the only Android users on the planet who found it incredibly tricky to highlight and copy the exact text line I need, but it appears to be a far more widespread issue.

As the Reddit post reads:

It’s such a lame part of the modern smartphone. I have asked Google about this and there is currently ‘no plans’ to improve how text is highlighted. This is so frustrating, and it’s not just an Android problem, I also have an iPhone for work and it’s even worse on that.

I couldn’t agree more.

Selecting text is a core part of the smartphone usage experience, whether it’s highlighting keywords in a website or selecting particular words to search or forward in messages.

I was a prolific Blackberry user in years past, and one of the most underrated features was the optical trackpad that appeared on several models. It allowed far more precision than modern touchscreens, and that’s the level of dexterity that many users crave today.

Android does offer users some mitigating tools to help adjust the selected text, including physically moving the cursor, adjusting it with a swipe on the Gboard spacebar, and various other gesture-based tweaks, but these actions take time. Arguably, these tools just aren’t enough.

But do you agree? Do you find it difficult to select text on Pixels, Galaxy phones, and other Android devices? How do you get around these limitations? Let’s discuss in the comments section.

• Users have been reporting Gemini using massive amounts of RAM in Chrome for over a year.

• Google hasn’t explained what was wrong or what it fixed.

If you use Gemini in Chrome, you may have noticed that it can slow your computer down to a crawl. Users have been complaining about Gemini’s RAM usage on the web for a long time, especially when it’s running in a Chrome tab. Fortunately, that may no longer be a problem.

Reddit user That_Discussion_7513 posted a screenshot of Gemini in Chrome using over 5GB of RAM on their PC. In a comment on their post, the official Google Support account said the issue has been resolved. It also asked users to report back if they still see high memory usage in Chrome. The company didn’t explain what was wrong or what it fixed.

That_Discussion_7513 / Reddit

The issue itself isn’t new, and the complaints go back a while. After digging through some Reddit posts, we found a thread from over a year ago showing a Gemini tab using 3.6GB of RAM. The user said memory use increased with session time rather than chat length. According to them, a chat with just five messages and a PDF attachment started at around 250MB and reached 900MB after 15 minutes.

There are several other reports peppered throughout the year as well. One user saw Gemini using 1.1GB in Chrome. Another reported 6.4GB of RAM being used by the Gemini web app, with usage peaking at 8.4GB.

Several commenters joked that the RAM usage by Gemini’s web app in Chrome makes it seem as if Gemini is running a local AI model in the browser. Chrome does install local AI models, but those use disk space and don’t sit in RAM.

Now that Google has confirmed the issue is fixed, you shouldn’t see Gemini using too much RAM in Chrome. However, we haven’t been able to independently verify the fix. You can check Gemini’s RAM usage in Chrome using Chrome’s Task Manager or the tab hover card. In case of any issues, you should report them to Google using Chrome’s built-in “Report an issue” option.

The best Black Friday deals for Android handhelds

Standout deals include the Retroid Pocket Duo Lite for just $99 and the powerful Odin 3 for $319.

TL;DR

• AYN, Retroid, and ANBERNIC have all revealed their Black Friday deals.

• AYN is offering the Odin 3 for $50 off, as well as $20 off the dual-screen Thor handheld.

• Retroid’s steepest discount is $50 off the Pocket Duo Lite, while ANBERNIC has discounts on the Rotate and two other devices.

Black Friday is almost upon us, and there are already plenty of deals to go around. Handheld makers are also getting in on the action, as ANBERNIC, AYN, and Retroid have all announced their Black Friday deals.

AYN Black Friday deals

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

AYN is offering discounts off selected models from today (November 26) to November 30. The steepest discount is $50 off the Odin 3 when you use the promo code BF$50OFF at checkout on the company website. That means you can get the base 8GB/128GB model for $319, all the way up to $559 for the 16GB/1TB variant. Either way, you’re getting the most powerful Android handheld on the market right now, as it’s basically running a Snapdragon 8 Elite chip.

AYN also offers the dual-screen Thor handhelds, and you can get $20 off the standard AYN Thor models when you use the promo code BF$20OFF. That means a starting price of just $309 for the 8GB/128GB variant. This discount doesn’t apply to the Lite model, though. Nevertheless, the standard model brings a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 chipset, a pair of OLED panels (including a 120Hz top screen), and a 6,000mAh battery.

Finally, the venerable Odin 2 Portal has also received a modest $10 discount with the promo code BF$10OFF. That’s a very small discount and only applies to the 8GB/128GB model, but those looking for a large yet relatively powerful device should still consider it. The handheld boasts a 7-inch 120Hz OLED screen, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor, an 8,000mah battery, and all the expected controls. It even (unofficially) supports Steam OS.

Retroid Black Friday deals

Rita El Khoury / Android Authority

Hoping for cheaper Retroid handhelds? You’re in luck, as the stalwart brand is also offering discounts of $10 to $50 on its various devices via its website. The most notable deal might be the 4GB/64GB Retroid Pocket Duo Lite for just $99 when you use the code BFSAVE$50 at checkout, which is a $50 saving. You can also get the 6GB/128GB model for $149 by using the code BFSAVE$20, which translates to a $20 discount.

Looking for a more capable dual-screen Retroid device? Then the company is offering the 8GB/128GB Pocket Duo for $249 if you use the BFSAVE$20 code at checkout. It stands out from the Lite model by offering a more powerful chip (effectively the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4), 120Hz OLED screens, and more RAM. The horsepower boost in particular makes this handheld more viable for 3DS emulation.

The firm’s cheapest device on Black Friday is the Retroid Pocket Classic for $79 (code: BFSAVE$20). The Pocket Classic is well worth a look at this price if you want a Game Boy-style Android handheld.

Retroid is also knocking $10 off its recently released Pocket Nova when you use BFSAVE$10 at checkout. That means you’re paying $229 for the 8GB/128GB model, all the way to $264 for the 12GB/128GB Crystal variant. Either way, you’re getting a 4:3 120Hz OLED screen and what is basically the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 processor.

The Pocket 6 has also received a $10 discount via the BFSAVE$10 code at checkout. That means the device now has a starting price of $234 for the 8GB/128GB model. Throw in the effectively rebadged Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 chip, 6,000mAh battery, and 120Hz OLED screen, and you’ve got a well-rounded device for the price.

Finally, the previous-generation Pocket 5 has received a price cut for the 12GB/128GB variant. It can be had for just $169 when you use the aforementioned $10 code at checkout. That’s not a huge saving, but it’s still well below the Pocket 6 price.

ANBERNIC Black Friday deals

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

ANBERNIC isn’t left out of the fun, either. The manufacturer is offering big and (very) small discounts on its various handhelds. These deals, which don’t require coupons, actually started on November 19 and are set to expire on December 3. One of the most notable promotions is a $16.23 discount on the swiveling RG Rotate, which was $94.99.

The company is also knocking $14.13 off the recently released RG 55G1. That means you’re paying just under $140 for this Switch Lite clone. Don’t expect to emulate Switch games here, but we found that the Snapdragon G1 Gen 2 chip could handle some GameCube and PS2 games.

The RG Vita has received a significant discount too, as you save $14.60 on the device. ANBERNIC is also knocking $16.20 off the Pro model if you want slightly more impressive specs.

TL;DR

• Goldgenie has launched customized Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra editions in 24K gold, rose gold, and platinum finishes.

• Prices start at £2,597 (~$3,400) for the S26 Ultra and £4,395 (~$5,757) for the Z Fold 8 Ultra.

• Both phones come with free worldwide shipping and a lifetime warranty on the customization.

For most people, choosing a new smartphone color comes down to whatever the manufacturer offers. But for those with deeper pockets, even Samsung’s most expensive phones have room for a little more luxury. Goldgenie has been turning Galaxy flagships into shiny status symbols since the days of the Galaxy S6, and more than a decade later, the company is giving the Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra a 24K gold makeover, just in time for Christmas.

Goldgenie has opened orders for customized versions of Samsung’s two flagships in three finishes: 24K gold, rose gold, and platinum. The latter uses rhodium, a precious metal in the platinum group. All three finishes feature a highly reflective, mirror-like appearance.

The customized Galaxy S26 Ultra starts at £2,597 (~$3,400), while the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra will set you back at least £4,395 (~$5,757). Goldgenie offers the former in 256GB, 512GB, and 1TB storage configurations, while the foldable is available in 512GB and 1TB variants.

These are genuine Samsung phones with cosmetic modifications, not hardware upgrades. Each comes with a luxury presentation case, a certificate of authenticity, and a lifetime warranty covering Goldgenie’s customization.

Goldgenie has previously given the Galaxy S20 series a similar makeover, but it’s hardly the only one in this business. Just last week, rival luxury customization company Caviar unveiled a GTA VI-inspired Galaxy Z Fold 8 series featuring two layers of 24K gold plating, with the Ultra model starting at an eye-watering $11,560.

By those standards, Goldgenie’s latest creations almost look like a bargain.

The company offers free worldwide shipping through DHL and says it dispatches orders within seven days. If you’re planning to put either of these golden Galaxies under someone’s Christmas tree, Goldgenie recommends placing your order by December 16.

items.summary: The dummy units show four rear cameras again, but it's unlikely to be the case.
items.body:

Mobile

Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra dummy units leaked in hands-on video

The dummy units show four rear cameras again, but it's unlikely to be the case.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 1:59 AM ET

•

•

Hadlee Simons / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• The upcoming Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra dummy units have leaked again in a new hands-on video.

• It shows the phone in white and black, with a redesigned camera island.

• The dummy units also show four cameras on the back, but it’s likely one of them will be the flash on the actual device.

We’re a few months away from the Galaxy S27 series going official, but the leaks aren’t slowing down. There’s a lot of excitement around Samsung’s upcoming flagship phones, and rightfully so, as early leaks have suggested several noticeable design changes. We’ve already seen leaked images of the S27 Pro and Ultra dummy units, and now we’re getting a much more detailed look.

YouTuber Jam Ancheta has posted a new video going hands-on with the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra dummy units. The video showcases the S27 Pro in black, while the S27 Ultra dummy unit is white. Both units have the same rear camera layout, set in the redesigned camera island.

Surprisingly, the dummy units seem to have four rear cameras. However, an earlier leak from Ice Universe suggested that both phones will instead come with a triple rear camera setup. That still seems more likely, since the dummy units don’t have an LED flash in the camera island. It’s possible that one of the dummy lenses will actually be an LED flash on the actual phone.

Also, according to the video, the Galaxy S27 Ultra could be about the same size as the iPhone 18 Pro Max, while the Galaxy S27 Pro is about the size of a standard iPhone 18 Pro. The phones could also continue using the same flat-frame design, volume and power buttons, and port setup as the Galaxy S26 series.

The video doesn’t offer any additional information about the phones’ hardware. However, previous leaks suggest the Galaxy S27 Pro could pack a 200MP primary camera, a 50MP ultrawide camera, and a 10MP telephoto lens with 3x optical zoom. The Galaxy S27 Ultra, on the other hand, could feature the same primary and ultrawide cameras, but pair them with an upgraded 50MP telephoto lens with 5x optical zoom. Either way, the cameras are likely to be a downgrade from the Galaxy S26 Ultra.

It’s worth noting that all of this information is unconfirmed at this point. Although it’s quite possible that Samsung’s upcoming flagships will look like this and use a similar camera setup, it’s best to take these details with a pinch of salt.

items.summary: Watch out for unexpected recovery emails and invitations.

1Password confirms hackers stole customer data, but not their passwords

Watch out for unexpected recovery emails and invitations.

•

TL;DR

• 1Password has confirmed a security breach that exposed some customers’ personal information, including names and email addresses.

• The company says no customer passwords were exposed and that users don’t need to change their account or saved passwords.

• 1Password recommends watching out for unexpected account recovery emails and invitations following the breach.

Trust is everything when you’re in the business of keeping people’s passwords safe. It’s a responsibility that has only grown for 1Password in recent months, with the company enabling Claude and, more recently, other AI agents to sign into websites without exposing users’ credentials. That trust is now being put to the test after 1Password confirmed a security breach that exposed some customer information, although it maintains that users’ passwords are safe.

In a blog post published on November 25, 1Password revealed that it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting suspicious activity involving an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker gained access to the company’s source code and compromised backend services, obtaining customer names, email addresses, account identifiers, and other account information.

However, 1Password maintains that neither customer vaults nor the encryption keys protecting them were compromised. The company doesn’t store your account password or Secret Key, so you don’t need to change your 1Password password or any passwords saved in your vault. The company says it has secured the affected systems, changed potentially exposed internal credentials, and strengthened its account recovery and invitation verification process. It hasn’t disclosed how many customers were affected.

This isn’t 1Password’s first security scare. In October 2023, the company disclosed an incident linked to a breach at Okta, although no customer data was accessed at the time. Rival LastPass suffered a more serious breach in 2022, with hackers eventually obtaining copies of customer password vaults. As recently as June 2026, LastPass suffered another data breach that exposed customers’ personal information but left their saved passwords untouched.

For now, 1Password users should be particularly wary of unexpected account recovery emails and invitations. Hackers could use the stolen information to make phishing attempts more convincing. So if the incident makes you uncomfortable sticking with 1Password, Android has a safer way to move passwords and passkeys between password managers without exporting your entire vault in plain text.

items.body: A MacBook Air with a new look could launch in late 2027 or 2028, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said in the latest episode of his Power On podcast. Apple plans to refresh the ‌MacBook Air‌ with M6 chips in early 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2, but that update won't include a new design. A more extensive overhaul could follow later in 2027 or in 2028, and the ‌MacBook Air‌ could get an OLED display at that time. MacBook Air is Apple's most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027, 2028 is when we're going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation. Apple last overhauled the ‌MacBook Air‌'s design in 2022, eliminating the prior wedge shape for a more uniform MacBook Pro-style chassis. The machine adopted a brighter Liquid Retina display with a notch for the camera, and a MagSafe charging port. In 2023, Apple added a 15-inch model, but since then, we've only gotten minor updates. Apple just added ‌OLED‌ to the MacBook Pro with the launch of the 2026 PROLED models, so it's not clear whether the high-end display will trickle down to the ‌MacBook Air‌ that quickly. In prior reports , Gurman has leaned more toward the 2028 timeline than late 2027. Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899, while the ‌MacBook Air‌ is one of Apple's more affordable notebooks and starts at $1,299. Apple would likely need to offer a high-end ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Air‌ alongside ‌MacBook Air‌ models with an LCD display to keep the price gap intact. Google Home is sorting out issues with speakers, cameras, lights, and more

TL;DR

• Google Home is getting some new features and fixes for speakers, cameras, lights, and thermostats.

• Home Premium users will no longer have to configure all their cameras separately.

• Google’s smoothing out issues with transferring music playback to a new speaker or display.

Big changes are on the way for your Google-powered smart home, with Assistant finally scheduled to go away for good next summer — that’s still months off, though, and in the meantime we’ve got a fresh batch of Google Home updates to check out.

Today Google’s sharing its latest set of new features and bugfixes coming to Home, and it looks like there are quite a few in here that are worth paying attention to. For starters, owners of those affordable Walmart Onn smart cameras can now use Familiar Faces with outdoor models. Other camera upgrades include support for clip feedback when multiple users are configured as admins, as well as manual controls for camera security sirens. We’re also getting bugfixes for event notification previews, event-based video history, and camera controls in landscape view.

Home Premium subscribers can look for a new onboarding flow when adding multiple cameras to their homes, letting you configure premium features all at once.

Setting up a Nest Thermostat? Google’s adding a new feature that lets you clone daily temperature settings, so you can quickly apply the same options across multiple days.

We’ve got a few fixes and improvements related to speakers incoming. Google Home Speaker setup should now proceed with fewer visual glitches, and Google’s resolved an issue with configuring these as stereo pairs. There’s also a handful of fixes for audio issues with Google TV, and you should notice more consistent behavior now when attempting to transfer music between different devices.

If you’ve ever run into problems choosing the perfect color for your RGB smart lights in Google Home on iOS, check out the updated color wheel now rolling out.

In addition to all these improvements to the Home app and smart device operation, Google also shared its latest Gemini for Home enhancements today.

TL;DR

• WhatsApp appears to be developing a system for eSIM discovery, purchase, installation, and management.

• Users would be able to search for eSIMs based on specific travel destinations.

• Automated tools could wait to activate the eSIM until you arrive where you’re headed.

WhatsApp just got a big upgrade with the announcement of support for scheduling messages, and now we’re already getting an early look at what could be coming next, as we uncover evidence for what looks like a new travel eSIM feature.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Looking across the changes present in WhatsApp’s version 2.26.47.10 update, we’re finding multiple references to “Travel eSIM” support. This isn’t yet live in the app, but here’s a preview for how one of the associated screens could be taking shape:

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

Internally, we’re seeing a whole lot of text strings that appear connected to this feature. Here are just a few:

Code

+Travel eSIM installed
+Keep WhatsApp open until it’s done.
+Installing travel eSIM…
+Getting your travel eSIM ready…
+Install it once and use with all your plans.
+Your travel eSIM is ready
+WhatsApp will add a travel eSIM to your phone. Your plan starts when your phone connects in %1$s.
+Install eSIM?
+This phone can’t take this eSIM. It may be locked to a carrier or out of eSIM space.
+Couldn’t install travel eSIM
+This eSIM’s activation code is invalid or has already been used.
+Couldn’t set up your travel eSIM
+Travel eSIMs aren’t available to you yet
+Your plan starts when you turn on your eSIM.
+Couldn’t load plans
+Loading data plans
+Plans aren’t available for this destination
+Your phone didn’t let WhatsApp install this eSIM.
+Installing an eSIM needs a phone with an eSIM chip and a recent version of Android.
+This phone can’t install eSIMs
+Install it now and turn it on when you arrive in %1$s.
+Your plan starts when your phone connects there. You’ll get a message when it does.

Based on what we’ve found so far, we can make a few guesses about how this is likely to operate. It seems that we’ll be able to enter a destination into the app, and WhatsApp would search for compatible eSIM options. Those may not be available for everyone, all at once, as we find “coming soon” messages prepared for both global and regional plans. Options may include fixed-data, as well as unlimited plans.

You can expect to see a few introductory screens helping to educate users about eSIMs, and it sure looks like the app is preparing to integrate with Android’s eSIM installation process.

One handy feature could be an automated system for turning on the eSIM only when we actually reach the destination we intended to use it — freeing us from accidentally plowing through our eSIM data before we really needed it.

Management tools should let you view the eSIMs you’ve purchased so far, seeing which are still available, which are expired, and which have data remaining on them. And along the way, it looks like the app will be able to give you low-data warnings or let you know when a plan is about to end.

Readers' poll

Would you use WhatsApp to buy and install eSIMs?

0 votes

Of course, there’s the possibility your phone may not support this functionality, especially if it’s running an older version of Android. For the moment, at least, we don’t yet have a clear sense for where that cutoff may lie, but expect there to be one.

Finally, WhatsApp might not be preparing this new support on its own, and a “Powered by %1$s” string could suggest that some of this eSIM system may arrive courtesy of a third-party service — we just don’t yet know whose name is going to show up in place of that variable.

All of this sounds pretty nice to our ears. Buying an eSIM is a great option for international travel, and WhatsApp is a great messaging service for travel abroad, so this feels like a match made in heaven. It also looks like WhatsApp is serious about its approach here, and the strings we’ve found paint the picture of quite robust integration. For now, we’ll keep looking for the rest of the details on how this new service offering could be coming together.

WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.

items: WhatsApp appears to be developing a system for eSIM discovery, purchase, installation, and management.
Users would be able to search for eSIMs based on specific travel destinations.
Automated tools could wait to activate the eSIM until you arrive where you’re headed.

blocks.text: WhatsApp just got a big upgrade with the announcement of support for scheduling messages, and now we’re already getting an early look at what could be coming next, as we uncover evidence for what looks like a new travel eSIM feature.
APK teardown
This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Looking across the changes present in WhatsApp’s version 2.26.47.10 update, we’re finding multiple references to “Travel eSIM” support. This isn’t yet live in the app, but here’s a preview for how one of the associated screens could be taking shape:
AssembleDebug / Android Authority
Internally, we’re seeing a whole lot of text strings that appear connected to this feature. Here are just a few:
Code

+Travel eSIM installed
+Keep WhatsApp open until it’s done.
+Installing travel eSIM…
+Getting your travel eSIM ready…
+Install it once and use with all your plans.
+Your travel eSIM is ready
+WhatsApp will add a travel eSIM to your phone. Your plan starts when your phone connects in %1$s.
+Install eSIM?
+This phone can’t take this eSIM. It may be locked to a carrier or out of eSIM space.
+Couldn’t install travel eSIM
+This eSIM’s activation code is invalid or has already been used.
+Couldn’t set up your travel eSIM
+Travel eSIMs aren’t available to you yet
+Your plan starts when you turn on your eSIM.
+Couldn’t load plans
+Loading data plans
+Plans aren’t available for this destination
+Your phone didn’t let WhatsApp install this eSIM.
+Installing an eSIM needs a phone with an eSIM chip and a recent version of Android.
+This phone can’t install eSIMs
+Install it now and turn it on when you arrive in %1$s.
+Your plan starts when your phone connects there. You’ll get a message when it does.

Based on what we’ve found so far, we can make a few guesses about how this is likely to operate. It seems that we’ll be able to enter a destination into the app, and WhatsApp would search for compatible eSIM options. Those may not be available for everyone, all at once, as we find “coming soon” messages prepared for both global and regional plans. Options may include fixed-data, as well as unlimited plans.
You can expect to see a few introductory screens helping to educate users about eSIMs, and it sure looks like the app is preparing to integrate with Android’s eSIM installation process.

One handy feature could be an automated system for turning on the eSIM only when we actually reach the destination we intended to use it — freeing us from accidentally plowing through our eSIM data before we really needed it.

Management tools should let you view the eSIMs you’ve purchased so far, seeing which are still available, which are expired, and which have data remaining on them. And along the way, it looks like the app will be able to give you low-data warnings or let you know when a plan is about to end.
Readers' poll
Would you use WhatsApp to buy and install eSIMs?
0 votes

Of course, there’s the possibility your phone may not support this functionality, especially if it’s running an older version of Android. For the moment, at least, we don’t yet have a clear sense for where that cutoff may lie, but expect there to be one.

Finally, WhatsApp might not be preparing this new support on its own, and a “Powered by %1$s” string could suggest that some of this eSIM system may arrive courtesy of a third-party service — we just don’t yet know whose name is going to show up in place of that variable.

All of this sounds pretty nice to our ears. Buying an eSIM is a great option for international travel, and WhatsApp is a great messaging service for travel abroad, so this feels like a match made in heaven. It also looks like WhatsApp is serious about its approach here, and the strings we’ve found paint the picture of quite robust integration. For now, we’ll keep looking for the rest of the details on how this new service offering could be coming together.

items.body: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account had been breached and began investigating. The company says the breached GitHub account was used to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, with the code downloading some customer data. Here's a list of what the hacker was able to get: Names and email addresses customers use to sign into 1Password Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (1Password says this can't be used for account access) Tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery Other non-secret account data related to 1Password's internal architecture, like version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers 1Password source code, which 1Password says does not include customer data or user secrets Access to 1Password's CI/CD system, which it says has infrastructure-related secrets for the service to work According to 1Password, there is no impact to its services, availability, or product security. Customer vaults and the items in them were not accessed, nor were the keys that protect vaults. The hacker did not have access to account recovery keys or 1Password apps and browser extensions. 1Password vaults are encrypted and protected by keys on the user end, so content is not accessible to 1Password or anyone who hacks the 1Password servers. The biggest risk comes from the token breach. Tokens can be used for account recovery, but they only work when paired with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit code sent to a user's email address. items.body: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a message can be done by pressing and holding the send button after composing and then choosing a date and time. Scheduled messages work with text, photos, and videos, and will still send even if a user's device is offline. There is an option to see all scheduled messages and delete them before they're sent if needed. Scheduled messages are end-to-end encrypted and look like any other WhatsApp message, with no indication on the receiver's end that the message was scheduled. Apple's iMessage service already has a Send Later feature that supports scheduling messages, so WhatsApp is catching up with Apple's built-in messaging option. WhatsApp says scheduled messages are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. items.summary: Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.

Gemini for Home gets faster responses, smoother chats, and fixes for follow-up and music bugs

Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.

•

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google has fully rolled out speed improvements for common Gemini for Home smart home commands.

• The latest update fixes bugs affecting follow-up commands and stopping media playback.

• Google is also rolling out an improved Gemini Live experience, more expressive storytelling, and web answer sources on supported smart displays.

The story of Gemini for Home’s transition from Google Assistant is beginning to take a more positive turn. We’ve seen some users warming up to Google’s new voice assistant, particularly after noticeable improvements in response times. Now, Google is giving Gemini more polish, whether you’re asking it to switch off the lights or tell your kids a bedtime story.

With its second November update, Google has confirmed that speed improvements for common smart home commands have fully rolled out to Gemini for Home Early Access users. So, whether you’re turning on the lights or adjusting the thermostat, Gemini should respond and act faster.

Google has also fixed a bug where Gemini would occasionally forget the context of a conversation. For example, asking Gemini to turn the living room lights back on shortly after telling it to turn them off should now work as expected. Another fix addresses an issue where Gemini would incorrectly insist that nothing was playing when asked to stop music or other media.

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Beyond these fixes, Google is beginning to roll out the upgraded Gemini Live experience it announced last week alongside energy-saving improvements for Nest thermostats and new features for Google Home cameras. Over the coming weeks, Google Home Premium subscribers will get faster, more natural conversations with Gemini, along with the ability to set timers, add reminders, and control smart home devices without ending an ongoing chat.

Gemini is also becoming a better storyteller. Starting today, stories will feature more expressive voices and varied pacing, and you can steer the plot as Gemini narrates. And if you own a supported smart display, you’ll be able to tap a new “Sources” option to see the websites Gemini used to answer your questions.

With Google Assistant set to retire from smart home devices in August 2027, every little improvement counts. And while more entertaining bedtime stories are a welcome addition, getting Gemini to remember which lights you were talking about is likely to make a bigger difference in everyday life.
